proposals.title: Expand definition of “sell” to cover free transfers

redline.before: “Sell,” “selling,” “sale,” or “sold,” means selling, renting, releasing, disclosing, disseminating, making available, transferring, or otherwise communicating orally, in writing, or by electronic or other means, a consumer’s personal information by the business to another business or a third party for monetary or other valuable consideration.
redline.after: “Sell,” “selling,” “sale,” or “sold,” means selling, renting, releasing, disclosing, disseminating, making available, transferring, or otherwise communicating orally, in writing, or by electronic or other means, a consumer’s personal information by the business to another business or a third party for monetary or other valuable consideration. The term also includes any transfer of a consumer’s personal information to a third party, regardless of whether monetary or other valuable consideration is exchanged, except where such transfer is permitted under the consumer‑directed disclosure exception of section 1798.140(t)(2)(A) or the service‑provider exception of section 1798.140(t)(2)(C).

proposals.rationale: The current definition of “sell” limits liability to transfers made for monetary or other valuable consideration, allowing businesses to hand off opted‑out consumers' data to ad networks for free. By expanding the definition to include any transfer of personal information to a third party, regardless of consideration, while preserving the consumer‑directed disclosure and service‑provider exceptions, the loophole is closed without prohibiting legitimate uses such as payment processing services or consumer‑requested data sharing.

lazy.title: Ban all post-opt-out disclosures (overbroad)

redline.before: from selling the consumer’s personal information after its receipt of the consumer’s direction, unless the consumer subsequently provides express authorization for the sale of the consumer’s personal information.
redline.after: from disclosing the consumer’s personal information to anyone after its receipt of the consumer’s direction.

lazy.rationale: A lazy, overbroad fix that bans every post-opt-out disclosure, including the service-provider payment processing and consumer-directed transfers the purpose contract requires to stay legal.
